site_vertical_uncertainty.evidence_basis: NASA PGDA product 78 labels Site01_final_adj_5mpp_toterr.tif as total Z uncertainty, formally the RMS error. A Site01 anchor uncertainty sampled from this raster therefore inherits RMS semantics rather than hard-bound semantics.

layers.evidence_basis: NASA PGDA product 78 explicitly describes the total-Z uncertainty raster as RMS error; Barker et al. describe contributions from interpolation, orbital, range and sampling error.

NASA PGDA product 90 labels LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ_ERR.TIF as surface-height error in meters. LL-009O does not promote that label to either RMS or hard-upper-bound semantics until the source methodology is explicitly bound and reviewed.

expected_result_before_further_closure.risk_qualified: blocked while any admitted layer remains semantics_class=unknown
expected_result_before_further_closure.descriptive_only: allowed if N/L/M byte and lineage bindings pass

required_follow_on: Resolve the statistical semantics of the large-area ADJ_ERR product from source methodology.
For RMS inputs, select and hash an explicit statistical or clone-ensemble policy rather than treating 1x RMS as a hard bound.
Rescan every admitted source pixel for any multiplier/quantile rule that can change which pixel is worst; do not operate only on LL-009L top-K output.
Keep continuous/subpixel terrain-support closure separate from vertical-error magnitude semantics.
non_claims: This policy intentionally blocks an unqualified deterministic horizon claim for the current Site01 evidence semantics.
The policy does not assign Gaussian tails or any other distribution to RMS error.
The policy does not claim the large-area surface-height-error raster has any probability interpretation until that interpretation is source-supported.
